body: Coverage in Pakistan was primarily captured using a Generation 3 trekker camera.
The national language is Urdu, written in an alphabet similar to Arabic but often with curvier fonts. English is also an official language and commonly seen on signage.

Pakistan uses short licence plates, and since all coverage is in Punjab, most plates have a green strip on the left. Fully green plates are also common, distinguishing them from India's typically long plates.
A large portion of coverage is within well-ordered Mughal gardens. These are often surrounded by stone walls and associated with old temples or fortresses.
Brightly coloured, baggy pants are a common sight on people in Pakistan. This can help differentiate from India, where pants are often tighter.
Street View coverage in Pakistan is extremely limited and confined to the Punjab province, focusing on major temples and tourist attractions.
A grey car with a visible right side can be found in hidden coverage around Lahore Fort. This coverage is not on the main Google Maps but appears in some community maps.
Hidden trekker coverage exists just south of Lahore Fort, featuring busy, narrow urban streets.
Lahore Fort is a large fortress in Lahore, with the iconic Alamgiri Gate being a prominent monument.
Inside Lahore Fort, there is a distinct road completely enclosed by tall red brick walls.
The Government College University of Lahore is recognizable by its distinctive Gothic architecture.
The Patiala Block of King Edward Medical University is a large, white colonial building with large white domes marked with black lines.
Kinnaird College for Women University primarily consists of traditional Pakistani red brick buildings and paths.
Coverage in Jallo, an eastern suburb of Lahore, is semi-urban in a poorer-looking area with a very thick haze.
The Bahria Grand Hotel in Lahore's southwestern suburbs is identified by a minigolf course out front and a cow statue at the entrance.
Northwest of Harappa, there is trekker coverage starting at the Harappa Museum, mostly on a very narrow concrete path.
Hiran Minar, a small temple located northwest of Sheikhupura, is uniquely surrounded by a small lake with only a single bridge connecting it to land.

Coverage in western Kasur near the shrine of Hazrat Baba Bulleh Shah is identifiable by a mosque with a large green dome and smaller green domes on its minarets, which are visible from most locations.
In Pākapattan, there is hidden coverage of a busy market street with a distinctive roof made of rugs.
West of the market in Pākapattan, you can find hidden coverage of a very busy-looking urban street.
North of the market street in Pākapattan, there is hidden coverage of a narrow alleyway.
Rohtas Fort, west of Jhelum, is recognizable by its nearly black fortress walls, which are often visible in the distance.
Coverage in Katas, north of Sargodha, is distinguished by its combination of a hazy sky and hilly terrain.
Patriata, northeast of Islamabad, is identifiable by its hilly forests of tall pine trees. Some coverage was uniquely captured from an aerial lift.
Coverage in Changa Manga Forest Park can be identified by a northeastern path angle and a narrow channel running alongside it.
